title: Gene expression
note: Genes are expressed in two steps: transcription copies DNA into RNA, and translation reads mRNA three bases (one codon) at a time to build a polypeptide. In eukaryotes, pre-mRNA is capped, given a poly-A tail, and spliced before it leaves the nucleus. Cells control which genes are expressed, mostly by controlling transcription.

read.title: From gene to protein, and when to bother
text: A gene is a stretch of DNA that carries instructions, but the instructions stay in the nucleus. To use them, the cell first transcribes the gene. RNA polymerase binds a promoter, opens the helix, and builds a strand of RNA complementary to the template strand. In eukaryotes this pre-mRNA is then processed: a modified guanine cap is added to the 5' end, a poly-A tail to the 3' end, and introns are spliced out. The mature mRNA leaves through a nuclear pore.

At a ribosome, translation begins at the start codon, AUG. Transfer RNAs, each carrying a specific amino acid, pair their anticodons with codons on the mRNA. The ribosome links each new amino acid to the growing chain and shifts along the message one codon at a time, until a stop codon releases the finished polypeptide.

Not every gene is needed in every cell or at every moment. Bacteria group related genes into operons that switch on or off together. In E. coli, the lac genes stay off until lactose is present and are fully on only when glucose, the preferred sugar, is scarce. Eukaryotes control genes at many levels, from how tightly DNA is packed around histones to how long an mRNA survives.
